records.name: Edinburgh Castle
records.description: A medieval fortress perched on an extinct volcanic plug dominating Edinburgh's skyline for centuries. Home to the Honours of Scotland (Crown Jewels), St Margaret's Chapel (oldest building in Edinburgh), Mons Meg cannon, and the Scottish National War Memorial. Offers panoramic views over the city.
records.hours: 9:30am–6pm (1 Apr–30 Sep); 9:30am–5pm (1 Oct–31 Mar); closed 25–26 Dec

records.name: Palace of Holyroodhouse
records.description: The official Scottish residence of the British monarch, located at the foot of the Royal Mile. A 16th-century palace with connections to Mary Queen of Scots and Bonnie Prince Charlie. Features royal apartments, the Throne Room, and Great Gallery. Includes access to the ruins of adjacent Holyrood Abbey.
records.hours: 9:30am–6pm (1 Apr–31 Oct); 9:30am–4:30pm (1 Nov–31 Mar); closed when Royals in residence

records.name: Holyrood Abbey
records.description: Ruined Augustinian abbey founded in 1128 by King David I. The abbey church stands as a roofless ruin adjacent to Holyrood Palace. Once a significant royal residence and site of major Scottish historical events. Access included with Palace of Holyroodhouse admission.
records.hours: Accessible via Palace of Holyroodhouse admission (same hours as Palace)

records.name: St Giles' Cathedral
records.description: A prominent Gothic building on the Royal Mile at the heart of medieval Edinburgh. Founded in the 12th century and closely associated with the Scottish Reformation and John Knox. Features a distinctive crown-shaped spire, magnificent stained glass windows, and the ornate Thistle Chapel. Has been a working church for nearly 900 years.

records.name: Greyfriars Kirk and Kirkyard
records.description: Historic church built in 1620 and burial ground dating back to 1562. Most famous as the resting place of Greyfriars Bobby, a faithful Skye Terrier. The kirkyard contains graves of notable Edinburgh residents and is renowned as one of the world's most haunted cemeteries. Also known for Harry Potter connections and the National Covenant signed here in 1638.

records.name: Canongate Kirk
records.description: Historic church built in 1691 with distinctive Dutch-style gable, designed by architect James Smith. Serves as the parish church for the Palace of Holyroodhouse and Edinburgh Castle. Features elegant white interior with pale blue paintwork and a Royal Pew. Kirkyard contains graves of notable figures including economist Adam Smith and philosopher Dugald Stewart.
records.address: 153 Canongate, Royal Mile, Edinburgh EH8 8BN, Scotland

records.name: St Mary's Episcopal Cathedral
records.description: Neo-gothic cathedral built in 1874 on Palmerston Place in the west end of Edinburgh. Features impressive Gothic architecture with striking spires and stained glass windows, including the magnificent stained glass Millennium Window by Scottish sculptor Paolozzi. Hosts various events and music evenings.

records.name: National Museum of Scotland
records.description: Scotland's largest museum with eight floors of exhibits covering Scottish history, natural world, art and fashion, design, science and technology, and world cultures. Features the Grand Gallery with Victorian architecture, Dolly the sheep (world's first cloned mammal), Egyptian galleries, Lewis Chessmen, Millennium Clock, and rooftop terrace with panoramic city views. Free admission to main collections.

records.name: Scottish National Gallery (The National)
records.description: National art gallery located on The Mound in central Edinburgh, housing Scotland's national collection. Features masterpieces by Rembrandt, Titian, Vermeer, Velázquez, and Impressionist artists. Includes newly opened Scottish galleries with works from 1800-1945, showcasing artists like Charles Rennie Mackintosh and the Glasgow Boys. Free admission.

records.name: Scottish National Gallery of Modern Art
records.description: One of three galleries in the National Galleries of Scotland. Located at Belford Road, housing Scotland's national collection of modern and contemporary art. Features contemporary artworks and cutting-edge exhibitions. Extensive sculptural works on grounds by Eduardo Paolozzi, Charles Jencks, and other major artists. Free admission.

records.name: Scottish National Portrait Gallery
records.description: World's first purpose-built portrait gallery, opened in 1889. Features Scotland's national collection of portraits comprising 3,000 paintings and sculptures and 25,000 prints and drawings. Housed in a striking red-sandstone Gothic Revival building. Showcases portraits of important Scottish figures throughout history. Free admission.

records.name: Surgeons' Hall Museums
records.description: Medical museum comprising three collections: Wohl Pathology Museum, History of Surgery Museum, and Dental Collection. Housed in 19th-century listed building on Nicolson Street. Displays include surgical instruments, specimens, and exhibits on Edinburgh's medical history, including Burke and Hare body snatching. Opened to public since 1832. One of Scotland's oldest museum collections.

records.name: Camera Obscura & World of Illusions
records.description: Edinburgh's oldest purpose-built visitor attraction, operating for over 150 years on Castlehill near Edinburgh Castle. Five-floor interactive exhibition featuring over 100 hands-on exhibits exploring optical illusions, light, colour, holograms, mirror mazes, and vortex tunnels. Historic Victorian rooftop Camera Obscura projects live moving images of Edinburgh onto viewing table. Rooftop viewing platform offers 360-degree city views.
records.address: 549 Castlehill, Royal Mile, Edinburgh EH1 2ND, Scotland

records.name: Dynamic Earth
records.description: World-class science centre and planetarium telling the epic story of planet Earth from the Big Bang to present day. Located at foot of Arthur's Seat near Scottish Parliament. Features 360-degree immersive galleries with interactive exhibits including real iceberg, simulated volcano and earthquake, tropical rainforest scenes, and full-dome planetarium shows. Modern architecture designed like giant white armadillo.

records.name: Princes Street Gardens
records.description: Most important public park in central Edinburgh, created in the 1820s after draining the Nor Loch. Spans nearly 40 acres between Edinburgh's Old Town and New Town. Features iconic views of Edinburgh Castle at western end and Scott Monument in East Gardens. Popular gathering place for locals and tourists. Divided into East and West sections by The Mound.

records.name: Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh
records.description: Expansive botanical garden comprising over 70 acres. Scientific and conservation centre for plants with diverse plant collections from around the world. Features multiple glasshouses designed to replicate different climate zones. Popular tourist attraction offering walking paths and educational displays about plant diversity and conservation.

records.name: The Meadows
records.description: Large public park in south Edinburgh, 63 acres. Once home to Borough-Loch. Popular with students, families, runners and cyclists. Located near university district. Features play areas, tennis courts, and community gardens with orchard and wildflower patches. Popular gathering spot especially in summer months.

records.name: Holyrood Park
records.description: Largest green space in Edinburgh with 650 acres of royal parkland. Created in 1541 on orders of James V. Contains hills, lochs, cliffs and plains. Home to Arthur's Seat (251m), Edinburgh's highest point and an extinct volcano. Features Salisbury Crags, Hunter's Bog, and multiple lochs including Duddingston Loch and Saint Margaret's Loch. Multiple walking paths suit all ability levels.

records.name: Arthur's Seat
records.description: Extinct volcano and highest point in Edinburgh at 251 metres above sea level. Located within Holyrood Park. Features a rocky, wild summit offering panoramic views across the city, Firth of Forth, and beyond. Popular hill walk with several routes of varying difficulty. Named possibly after King Arthur, though origins are uncertain.

records.name: Calton Hill
records.description: Iconic viewpoint and public park at east end of Princes Street. Volcanic hill 103 metres above sea level. Home to neoclassical monuments including the unfinished National Monument (resembling Greek Parthenon), Nelson Monument (completed 1816), Dugald Stewart Monument, and Old Observatory House. UNESCO World Heritage Site offering panoramic views of Edinburgh Castle, Arthur's Seat, Old Town, Pentland Hills, and Firth of Forth.

records.name: Scott Monument
records.description: Victorian Gothic monument in Princes Street Gardens dedicated to Scottish author Sir Walter Scott. Standing 61.11 metres (200 feet) high, it is the world's second-largest monument to a writer. Designed by George Meikle Kemp. Visitors can climb 287 spiral steps to reach four viewing platforms offering 360-degree panoramic views of Edinburgh and surroundings. Includes museum room about Scott's life and legacy.
records.address: Princes Street Gardens, Edinburgh EH2 2EJ, Scotland

records.name: Scottish Parliament Building
records.description: Striking modern parliament building opened in 2004 at Holyrood, designed by Spanish architect Enric Miralles. Located at foot of Royal Mile opposite Palace of Holyroodhouse. Constructed from Scottish materials including granite, steel, and oak. Visitors can explore public areas free of charge, including the dramatic Main Hall and Debating Chamber from public gallery. Offers 10-minute talks and 45-minute guided tours.

records.name: The Real Mary King's Close
records.description: Underground network of 17th-century streets preserved beneath Edinburgh's Royal Mile, uninhabited for 400 years. Buried beneath the Royal Exchange building on the Royal Mile. Visitors descend into preserved alleyways, houses and shops from the 1600s-1700s. Guided character tours reveal stories of real residents, plague history, and Edinburgh's hidden past. Named after prominent 17th-century businesswoman Mary King.

records.name: Royal Yacht Britannia
records.description: Former floating palace of Queen Elizabeth II berthed in Port of Leith. Served the British Royal Family for 44 years, sailing over 1 million nautical miles on nearly 1,000 official visits. Visitors explore five accessible decks including State Rooms, Royal Apartments, Throne Room, and crew quarters with included audio guide in 36 languages. Rated Tripadvisor's No.1 UK Attraction.
records.station: Edinburgh Waverley (then bus to Leith Ocean Terminal)
records.address: Ocean Terminal, Leith, Edinburgh EH6 6JJ, Scotland

records.name: Edinburgh Zoo
records.description: Scotland's largest wildlife attraction and leading conservation centre. Covers 82 acres on Corstorphine Hill. Home to over 2,500 animals from around the world including penguins, koalas, giraffes, tigers, chimpanzees, and rare endangered species. Features Europe's largest outdoor penguin pool and the innovative Budongo Trail chimpanzee enclosure. Founded in 1913 by Royal Zoological Society of Scotland.

records.name: Glenkinchie Distillery
records.description: Historic Lowland whisky distillery located in Pencaitland just outside Edinburgh. Offers tours showcasing whisky production process and visitor facilities. Accessible as part of whisky tours from Edinburgh city centre. Features relaxing ambiance and professional tour guides explaining whisky-making traditions.
records.station: Pencaitland (no train); nearest = Edinburgh Waverley (then drive/bus 15 miles)

records.name: Holyrood Distillery
records.description: Modern whisky distillery located in Edinburgh city centre near Arthur's Seat, opened in 2019. Focuses on Edinburgh's distilling history with tours and tastings. Created a smoky cask offering inspired by Edinburgh's nickname 'Auld Reekie' (Old Smoky). Offers interactive experiences and abundant tour options with various tasting menus.

records.name: Port of Leith Distillery
records.description: World's tallest whisky distillery located in Leith, Edinburgh's historic port district. Features striking contemporary architecture visible across the harbour. Offers 90-minute distillery tours showcasing vertical production layout. Visitors fill and label their own bottle of New Make spirit. Includes tastings of grains, malts, blends and single casks. Rooftop bar with panoramic views.

records.name: The Scotch Whisky Experience
records.description: Whisky experience attraction located on the Royal Mile showcasing Scotland's whisky heritage. Not a working distillery but offers informative tours covering all aspects of Scotch whisky production and traditions. Features tastings, live traditional Scottish music every evening, and dining options. Interactive exhibits and multimedia presentations about whisky regions.
